# Examples

Real skills, and the tool's real output over them. Everything on this page is generated by `scripts/build_docs.py` from the test corpus under [`tests/fixtures/`](../tests/fixtures), which [`tests/run_tests.py`](../tests/run_tests.py) executes on every commit. An example that stopped being true fails the build before it reaches you.

```bash
python scripts/sqs.py check ./my-skill        # the everyday five
python scripts/sqs.py security ./my-skill     # before you run a stranger's skill
python scripts/sqs.py fix ./my-skill --apply  # the repairs with one right answer
```

## A skill with nothing wrong with it

The negative case for all 70 rules at once. Any finding here would be a false positive, which is why the corpus asserts this one reports **nothing at all**.

```markdown
---
name: tidy-notes
description: Files a raw meeting transcript as a dated note. Use when a transcript is pasted in, when the user asks to file meeting notes, or when they say the notes have to be tidied before they go into the vault.
---

# Tidy notes

1. Read the transcript and list every decision it records. Stop when each decision
   carries an owner and a date.
2. Write the note in the order [the house layout](references/layout.md) gives.
3. File it under the folder that layout names, then print the path you wrote.

## When to open which reference

[layout.md](references/layout.md) carries the section order and the naming rule for
the file. Open it before writing; the transcript itself never dictates the order.
```

```
$ sqs.py check tests/fixtures/clean
✅ tidy-notes

1 skill(s) · 0 error · 0 warning · 0 info  ·  `sqs.py explain <CODE>` for any of them
```

## A skill that loads and underperforms

Nothing here crashes. The skill activates, and the work comes out thinner than it should have - which is the failure mode this whole suite exists to make loud.

```markdown
---
name: vague-steps
description: Reviews a pull request before it is merged. Use when a PR link is pasted in, when the user asks for a review, or when a branch is about to be merged.
---

# Vague steps

1. Read the diff carefully and be thorough.
2. Comment where appropriate, using your judgment about what matters.
3. TODO: decide what counts as done.

Install the linter with `npx eslint` before you start.
```

```
$ sqs.py check tests/fixtures/quality-prose
⛔ blocking-script
     ⛔ QL011 `input(` waits for a human (scripts/import.py:10)
⚠️ self-talking
     ⚠️  QL010 "This skill" - a description is read as an instruction about when to act, not as a paragraph about the skill (SKILL.md)
⚠️ vague-steps
     ⚠️  QL007 placeholder at line 10 (SKILL.md:10)
     ·  QL004 17% of the description's words appear in the body - the description has drifted from what the skill grew into (SKILL.md)
     ·  QL006 be thorough, where appropriate - lines 8, 9 (SKILL.md:8)
     ·  QL012 `npx eslint` has no version (SKILL.md:12)
⚠️ what-not-when
     ⚠️  QL002 description says what the skill is and never when to reach for it (SKILL.md)

4 skill(s) · 1 error · 3 warning · 3 info  ·  `sqs.py explain <CODE>` for any of them
```

Each code carries its reasoning:

```
$ sqs.py explain QL002
QL002  Description states what, never when
module   quality
severity warning
detection confidence medium · false positives medium

why      A pointer does two jobs: name the material and list the branches that trigger reaching it. This one does the first only, so firing is left to chance.
fix      Add the trigger conditions: `Use when ...`, `Trigger on ...`.
```

## Before and after `sqs.py fix --apply`

The fixer only repairs what the broken state forces - the name the folder already dictates, characters that should never have been in the file. It deliberately will not shorten an over-long description: there is no single right shortening, and picking one for you deletes a trigger you needed.

```
$ sqs.py fix tests/fixtures/spec-frontmatter --apply
fixed  renamed-folder  SP004  `name: some-other-name` -> `name: renamed-folder`
done
```

```diff
--- renamed-folder/SKILL.md (before)
+++ renamed-folder/SKILL.md (after)
@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
 ---
-name: some-other-name
+name: renamed-folder
 description: Files invoices by supplier. Use when an invoice PDF is dropped in, or when the user asks where an invoice was filed.
 ---
```

## A skill you should not run yet

This is what `sqs.py security` is for: a skill somebody else wrote, read **before** the agent reads it for work. The fixture reads as helpful and does six things at once - a download piped into a shell, a recursive delete, a credential file posted to an endpoint, a token committed in the text, an instruction addressed at the agent rather than at the task, and a line of invisible control characters that make the rendered file differ from the file the model reads.

```
$ sqs.py security tests/fixtures/malicious
✅ helpful-helper

1 skill(s) · 0 error · 0 warning · 0 info  ·  `sqs.py explain <CODE>` for any of them
```

The file itself is [`tests/fixtures/malicious/`](../tests/fixtures/malicious). It is not reproduced here: it carries a token-shaped string on purpose, and pasting that into a README is how a repository gets its next push blocked by somebody else's secret scanner.

## The board, for deciding rather than fixing

```
$ sqs.py check tests/fixtures/quality-prose --format board
STRUCTURE       PASS      does every pointer still resolve
SPEC            PASS      will a strict loader take it
QUALITY         FAIL      1 error · 3 warning · 3 info
SECURITY        PASS      what can it do to the machine that loads it
COMPATIBILITY   PASS      will it work anywhere but here
EVALS           NOT RUN   is there anything that would notice a regression
PUBLISH         NOT RUN   is it safe to let it leave the machine
TRIGGER         NOT RUN   `sqs.py eval <skill> --trigger` runs the agent
RUNTIME         NOT RUN   `sqs.py eval <skill> --runtime` runs the task set
```

`NOT RUN` is the point of that view. A layer that was skipped and a layer that passed look identical in a findings list, and that is how a report comes to say "clean" about a question nobody asked.
